newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees larger 97/98 world coffee surplus at 4 ml.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees larger 97/98 world coffee surplus at 4 ml.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) now sees a world 1997/98 coffee surplus at 4.0 million 60-kg bags, up from its earlier estimate of 1.9 million, and compared with a 2.0 million surplus in the current 1996/97 season.
The EIU kept its world 1997/98 consumption estimate largely unchanged at 75.7 million but it revised upward exportable production figure to 79.7 million from 77.5 million previously.
Coffee experienced a supply deficit of 7.6 million in 1995/96.
The EIU said in its latest quarterly world commodity forecast the larger surplus in 1997/98 would have bearish price implication especially for robustas.
The London-based group said the upward revision in exportable production reflected higher estimates from several key robusta suppliers especially Ivory Coast and Vietnam.
The weather has been generally good for the development of Indonesia's 1997/98 harvest (March/April).
The EIU maintained its forecast for Brazilian crop at 26-27 million, the same as 1996/97.

"Although yields are expected to be slightly lower for cyclical reasons, we expect this to be offset by the new bushes coming into production and the complete recovery of those in Parana from the 1994 frost damage," it said.
Brazil would have an exportable production of 17.5 million bags in 1997/98 against 16.80 million in 1996/97.
The EIU put the coming Colombian exportable crop at 12.5 million against 11.2 million this season.
